structured_output.content:
The regression was in `_make_quote_map()` in boltons/urlutils.py: the safe/unsafe branches were inverted, so characters that WERE in `safe_chars` got percent-encoded while unsafe characters were left literal. This caused normal path/query/fragment text (e.g. 'answer.py', 'e-shops.aspx') to come out fully percent-encoded, matching the reported regression (`'http://googl.../e-shops.aspx' == 'http://googl...E%61%73%70%78'`).

Fix applied: swapped the condition so that characters in `safe_chars` remain literal and all others get percent-encoded (`%XX`), restoring correct round-trip/query-param/IRI behavior.

Verified with a quick manual script: `URL('http://google.com/support/jdfi/bin/answer.py?answer=1234&hl=en-e-shops.aspx').to_text()` now returns the URL unchanged instead of fully percent-encoding every character, confirming the fix. No test directory was present in this checkout to run the full hidden suite, but the fix directly addresses the reported assertion and the root-cause logic inversion.

Swapped the condition so safe_chars map to themselves and all other characters map to their %XX percent-encoding. Verified manually that URLs now round-trip correctly via to_text().
